summary: A square granite tower on a wave-swept rock six miles off Crescent City, built 1883-1891 at a cost of over $700,000 and manned until 1975; now restored by a preservation society.

lens.where: Del Norte County Historical Society Museum, Crescent City

access.note: On a rock six miles offshore; reached by the preservation society's helicopter tours (tower open during them); can be seen from Point St. George. Tour availability may have changed.

facts.agency: St. George Reef Lighthouse Preservation Society (leased from Del Norte County; sources differ on title)

events.note: Steamer Brother Jonathan lost on St. George Reef
Land on Point St. George reserved 8 June 1866
Rocky islets off Point St. George reserved 9 January 1867
Northwest Seal Rock chosen as the site; $50,000 appropriated
Construction began; working party reached the rock in April 1883
Tower completed by end of October 1891; three keepers left in charge in November
12-inch steam whistle, in duplicate, first sounded 1 December 1891
First-order Fresnel lens installed August 1892 (NRHP)
First-order light established 20 October 1892
First assistant keeper William Erickson lost with the station boat, 17 October 1893
Fog signal changed 1 March 1895 to 5-second blasts, 75-second intervals, to save water and steam
Derrick erected on the wharf at Crescent City to lift the launch out of the water
Serious accident at the landing; derrick boom replaced by a 90-foot boom
Oil vapor lamp replaced the wick lamp
Steam whistle replaced by compressed-air sirens
Radiotelephone to Crescent City placed in commission 25 October 1923
Storm of 7 December 1923 wrecked the donkey engine house and hoisting gear
Sirens replaced by an air-powered diaphone
Harbor wharf at Crescent City leased as the launch landing
Lighthouse Bureau became part of the Coast Guard; enlisted crews replaced keepers
Launch accident of 5 April 1951: three Coast Guardsmen died
Tower interiors remodeled
Disestablished as a manned station 13 May 1975
Lens taken to Del Norte County museum (NRHP says 1975; Lighthouse Friends says 1983)
Listed 9 December 1993 (NRIS 93001373)
Relit as a private aid to navigation 20 October 2002; failed after a short time
Lit again 10 March 2012

corrections.why: The tower was finished in autumn 1891 and a steam whistle began 1 December 1891, but the Light-House Board lists the first-order light as established on 20 October 1892 (the lens arrived from Europe after the tower was done); USLHS's 1891 is the station's completion year.
Construction ran 1883-1891 and the tower was complete at the end of October 1891; 1892 is the year the light and lens came into service.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give 1891 (construction completed, fog whistle from 1 December 1891) and 1892 (lens installed August 1892 per the NRHP nomination; light shown 20 October 1892 per the Light-House Board and Putnam). The year the light first shone is 1892.

notes_for_editor: Rich on construction (Light-House Board 1892 appendix, NRHP) and on storm and fog-signal reports; thin on named keepers other than Olsen and Roux, whom the USLHS roster and its Roux page cover. Roster is USLHS/Kraig Anderson only, not independently checked against NARA registers; it runs to 1975 and includes Coast Guard crew names as the archive prints them. Matched by position/OCR: the Heuer appendix is OCR with garbled passages (the date of the rigger's death in 1891 is illegible: 'JniU; 16' could be June or July, so the story gives no month); the story's scan-page references for the Light-House Board volumes are archive.org scan pages, with printed pages given where the OCR page index agreed (pp. 187-188, 188, 168, 18, 16, 10 are from the printed numbers in the OCR and should be checked against the page images: the corpus tool marks several of them '?'). Disagreements stated in the story: Brother Jonathan toll (NRHP 166 lost vs Lighthouse Friends 244 aboard, 19 escaped); lens/light date (NRHP Aug 1892 installed vs Board Oct 20 1892 lit); flash interval (NRHP 12.5 s vs Lighthouse Friends 15 s); William Erickson's loss (Board and USLHS 1893 vs Lighthouse Friends 1895 on a trip to Crescent City, NRHP 'attempting to land'); lens removal (NRHP 1975 vs Lighthouse Friends 1983); preservation society founding (PBS 1986 vs Lighthouse Friends 1988); lease date (Lighthouse Friends 1996 vs 1995); title (Lighthouse Friends says both society-owned and leased from the county). NRHP calls the Brother Jonathan a schooner; Lighthouse Friends and others call her a steamer. The 1893 Hawaiian Gazette item is unsigned and has errors (1863 for the wreck, four keepers, no families); used only as a flagged period impression. The 1951 launch accident details and the 1909 pig story, 1896 blacksmith shop, 1937 59-day storm and Roux's recollection come from Lighthouse Friends only (copyrighted; paraphrased, one short quotation); the Del Norte Triplicate 1939 notice is read as transcribed on the USLHS page. The Wikipedia page was used for leads only and is not cited. The USLHS page for Roux gives 'Died 1939'; the Triplicate says he died the Monday after the attempt. Putnam 1917 pp. 239-240 is cited as general context only. Current ownership and tour availability should be re-checked with the society (stgeorgereeflighthouse.us redirects to a domain that did not resolve when checked). Access: Coast Guard-era names of living persons were not added beyond the roster lines the archive prints.
